# Data-Driven Yield Forecasting Benefits

By Lina Kovak, Data Scientist, Verdant Heights Indoor Farms

When Verdant Heights first installed our grow towers three years ago, we relied heavily on manual observation and historical averages to estimate weekly yields. Although this approach worked reasonably well, it often led to unexpected shortages or surpluses that challenged our distribution teams. It was only after we integrated predictive yield models into our operations that we saw a transformational improvement.

Predictive models use continuous sensor data—like nutrient dosing levels, temperature, humidity, and light cycles—combined with historical harvest records to forecast crop outputs days or weeks ahead. At Verdant Heights, implementing such models increased our forecast accuracy from about 70% to nearly 90%. This improvement enabled us to better align planting schedules with market demand, optimize labor allocation, and reduce waste.

One concrete benefit was during last summer’s unexpected heatwave. The models anticipated a dip in yield due to increased transpiration rates and adjusted nutrient profiles, allowing our team to proactively tweak dosing schedules. This mitigated what could have been a 15% drop in harvest volume down to under 5%.

For indoor farms looking to enhance operational planning, I recommend starting with a pilot project focused on one crop and one grow tower. Collect detailed environmental and dosing data, then work closely with data scientists to build and validate predictive models. Iterative refinement and close coordination with farming staff are key to turning forecasts into actionable insights.

Data-driven yield forecasting is no longer a futuristic concept—it’s a vital tool for indoor farms aiming to maximize efficiency and meet growing market demands consistently.
